sources.title: J. L. Guermond, P. Minev, and J. Shen, An overview of projection methods for incompressible flows
sources.locator: §§2.1–2.2, 3.1–3.3, and §8, printed pp. 6011–6015 and 6030–6032: projection, incremental and rotational corrections, boundary caveats, and inf-sup context.
sources.source_kind_detail: Full 35-page author-hosted survey PDF retrieved; the cited sections and their surrounding derivations were inspected in full.

contents.name: §§2.1–2.2, Helmholtz decomposition and projection setting
contents.support: The local proof establishes the finite-grid adjoint decomposition and orthogonal projection directly; the survey supplies the continuous projection context.

contents.name: §3.1, pressure Poisson projection step
contents.support: The periodic discrete pressure solve and exact divergence cancellation are stated and proved with the batch's fixed staggered signs.

contents.name: §3.2, incremental pressure-correction predictor and pressure increment
contents.support: The algorithm records the backward-Euler incremental update; its separate local theorem verifies well-definedness and the energy proof derives the identity.

contents.name: §3.2, smooth-data velocity accuracy and splitting-order caveat
contents.support: The local periodic staggered proof gives the displayed O(h^2+k) velocity estimate and states no pressure rate or wall rate.

contents.name: §3.2 and Remark 3.2, artificial Neumann pressure condition and tangential wall defect
contents.support: The B-page example solves a specific channel Poisson problem and computes the nonzero corrected tangential trace.

contents.name: §3.3, standard BDF2 and rotational pressure-correction formulas
contents.support: Both variants are defined with their pressure gauges and correction coefficient; no unproved rate is imported.

contents.name: §8, discrete inf-sup condition and pressure-correction analysis
contents.support: The local Schur theorem displays and proves the exact inf-sup, continuity, and stiffness constants used; the survey contributes context only.

contents.name: §2.1.3, central-difference approximation formulas
contents.support: The local Taylor proof gives the face and cell locations, pointwise remainders, and mass-norm estimate explicitly.

contents.name: §2.3.1, staggered pressure projection and divergence cancellation
contents.support: The local result proves exact divergence cancellation, the gauge, and orthogonality for the stated periodic grid.

contents.name: §2.3.2, pressure update in the fractional step

sources.title: Michele Benzi, Gene H. Golub, and Jörg Liesen, Numerical solution of saddle point problems
sources.locator: §§3.1–3.2 and §§10.1.1, 10.1.3, printed pp. 14–17 and 61–71: block factorization, Schur complement, exact block-diagonal eigenvalues, and steady Stokes mass-Schur scaling.
sources.source_kind_detail: Full 137-page author-hosted saddle-point survey PDF retrieved; all cited sections and their complete derivations were inspected.
sources.not_read: The complete PDF was retrieved; this entry claims mathematical reading only of the listed sections and their immediately surrounding proof text, not of unrelated sections.

contents.name: §3.1, block factorization through the leading block
contents.support: The local proof instantiates the published block-LU identity, proves the positive Schur matrix, and verifies both saddle equations.

contents.name: §3.2, Schur complement positivity and inf-sup connection
contents.support: The batch proves both quadratic-form bounds from the exact continuity, inf-sup and stiffness constants stated in its hypotheses.

contents.name: §10.1.1, block-diagonal symmetric-preconditioning eigenvalue polynomial
contents.support: The local proof derives the two-dimensional eigenvalue polynomial for each normalized Schur eigenmode and counts the unit eigenvalues.

contents.name: §10.1.1, scalar exact-Schur example
contents.support: The B-page example substitutes the scalar matrices and computes the golden-ratio roots and exact solution.

contents.name: §10.1.3, steady Stokes pressure-mass Schur equivalence under LBB stability
contents.support: The local MINI corollary derives the viscosity constants from Korn, pointwise divergence continuity and the actual Fortin inf-sup bound.

contents.name: §10.1.3, unsteady shifted-Schur scaling distinction
contents.support: The page and corollary explicitly restrict the mass-Schur estimate to the steady velocity stiffness and infer no unsteady shifted bound.

alternatives.argument: The carrier gives the complete backward-Euler incremental scheme with fixed periodic signs and gauge; the local well-definedness, projection and energy proofs verify its mathematical uses independently of the candidate.
Both BDF2 updates are defined with their exact correction coefficient, pressure gauge and well-definedness supplier; no rate or stability claim is imported from the candidate.
The complete local proof derives negative adjointness, the mean-zero Poisson solve, orthogonal projection onto ker D_h, and exact divergence cancellation from the fixed periodic operators.

The complete local argument proves second-order sampling consistency, reduces the corrected step to backward Euler on the divergence-free kernel, and sums a contractive error recurrence to obtain only the stated periodic velocity rate.
The B-page carrier solves an explicit Neumann Poisson equation, verifies both wall derivatives, and computes a strictly nonzero tangential trace; it makes no convergence-rate claim.
